messages:
Priya: Heads-up — need to lock the PRD acceptance criteria for the embeddings+rerank rollout. Customer asks include a dim change (1536 -> 768), different normalization defaults, and stricter batch semantics. I sketched an MVP vs stretch scope below, please react with concerns.

Priya: MVP proposals:
- Support dual-indexing: keep legacy 1536 index and new 768 index in parallel.
- API returns versioned embed_id, client chooses which index.
- Server-side on-the-fly projection NOT included in MVP.
- Default: L2-normalized outputs for both indices.
- Launch criteria: no >1% top-1 rerank regression on sampled prod queries, 99p latency delta <10ms, backfill <24h for active index subset.

Priya: Stretch ideas:
- Automatic auto-projection for mixed-dim queries.
- Transparent migration path: upstream re-ranking model accepts both dims with learned projection.
- Full backfill for all historical docs.

Sam: +1 on keeping projection out of MVP. that complexity blows up QA surface.
Sam: Add acceptance criteria: A/B test with at least 50k query samples and a predefined prompt set; human-eval on 200 cases for edge behaviors. Also require embedding cosine distribution sanity check (mean/std) within X tolerance.

Devin: Edge cases: what do we do for mixed-dim queries (client sends 768 query but targets are 1536 index)? If we force client to pick index, that breaks a lot of customers.
Devin: Options: 1) API rejects mixed dims with 400 + guidance, 2) server projects 768->1536 (or vice versa) with heuristics, 3) dual-embed lookup + score fusion. each has tradeoffs.

Mia: For customers with large corpora we can't do full backfill MVP. We should prioritize "active" docs (last 90d) and provide a backfill ETA window and progress metrics in Console. ops cost estimation?

Aj: Ownership/rollback: who runs the canary? product + eng-ml together. Rollback triggers: >1% top-1 regression OR >5% increase in P50 latency OR errors >0.5% for rerank endpoints. Need named owners in PRD.

Sam: Also call out batching semantics acceptance criteria: batching must not mix normalized and non-normalized payloads in the same batch. If we accept both modes, runtime should split batches by normalization-state so scores are comparable. Add a unit + integration test that sends mixed messages and verifies batching split.

Devin: Good catch. And ensure kv-cache behavior for chained rerank calls is consistent across dims — e.g., caching embeddings keyed by (doc_id, version) not just doc_id. Add that to acceptance criteria.

Priya: Agreed. I'll add the following to PRD acceptance checklist:
- Canaries + A/B with sample size thresholds (Sam's numbers).
- Quality gate: top-1 rerank delta <= 1% on holdout set + manual eval pass.
- Perf gate: 99p latency delta <10ms, P50 < configured SLO, error rate <0.5%.
- Backfill plan: active docs first (90d), progress dashboard, customer opt-in for full backfill.
- Batch semantics: runtime splits by norm-state and dim, tests included.
- Cache keying: versioned keys.

Mia: For Console: expose "index versions" UI, backfill ETA, and per-route cost estimate for dual-indexing. customers will ask about cost immediately.

Aj: Add acceptance test: simulate a spike (2x traffic for 30m) to validate autoscaling for Dedicated pools. Must not exceed budgeted burst capacity for customers on dedicated plans.

ops-bot: test-run scheduled: rerank-canary-suite on staging at 2025-05-09T18:00Z (ops id #9872).

Priya: Thanks — I'll draft the PRD sections and push a draft RFC by EOD. If anyone wants items moved from stretch -> MVP, speak up now.

Sam: Please include a short rollback playbook snippet in the PRD: how to pin clients to legacy index, API flags to force legacy, and metrics to watch.

Devin: One more tiny edge case: normalization differences can cause ties in top-k. Add acceptance criteria for tie-breaking determinism (stable sort by doc_id for equal scores).

Priya: Noted. I'll add deterministic tie-break and a small regression test set for tie cases.

Mia: ok to close this thread once PRD pushed. I'll review Console bits.

Aj: I'll own the rollout runbook.

Priya: Great — thanks everyone.
